serverFencing.mechanism: leader-local fencing token minted on every (re)invoke; invoker effects echo token; stale-token effects are dropped at write time

sdkInvocationIdentity.invocationId: ctx.request().id is stable across retries and suspensions
sdkInvocationIdentity.attemptHeaders: attempt-specific, but no stable documented fencing-token header was identified
sdkInvocationIdentity.attemptCompletedSignal: aborted when the current attempt ends

sdkAttemptTermination.mechanism: handler/interceptor execution is raced against attempt termination; connection abort poisons the VM and attempt-end rejects the execution path

t5Assessment.reason: The supported SDK terminates/races out the old handler when the attempt ends. Forcing a post-fencing stale protocol effect would require raw service-protocol construction or internal instrumentation, neither admitted by the current benchmark contract.

notes: Static server source is support for the fencing claim, not runtime evidence.
The server BSL 1.1 licensing gate remains separate from technical qualification.
A future protocol-level T5 profile would require an explicit methodological amendment before use.
